content_units: 21-Day Statistics Pass Plan

You have   28.5 total study hours  :   90 minutes on weekdays   and   3 hours on weekends  . The strongest plan for an intro stats exam is   practice-first  , with short concept review, daily retrieval, and repeated mixed problem sets in the final week.
3-Week Study Roadmap
Week   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz
Week 1   Days 1-7   Probability + core distributions   Short review; worked examples; targeted drills; formula sheet start   Solve basic probability and distribution questions accurately
Week 2   Days 8-14   Confidence intervals + hypothesis testing   Procedure practice; interpretation drills; decision rules; mixed sets   Choose the right test and explain results clearly

Week 3   Days 15-21   Correlation + simple linear regression + full revision   Regression interpretation; mixed timed sets; error log review; mock exams   Perform under time pressure and avoid repeat mistakes
Day-by-Day Study Schedule
Day 1: Probability foundations
- Review: sample space, events, unions, intersections, complements, conditional probability.
- Practice: 20-25 basic probability problems.
- Finish with: 10-minute recall of key formulas and notation.
- Goal: translate word problems into symbols correctly.
Day 2: Independence and Bayes-style reasoning
- Review: independence vs mutually exclusive; tree/table setups; Bayes intuition.
- Practice: 18-22 problems, especially conditional probability.
- Finish with: 5 missed-problem corrections.
- Goal: stop confusing \(P(A \mid B)\) with \(P(B \mid A)\).
Day 3: Random variables and expected value
- Review: discrete random variables, mean, variance, standard deviation.
- Practice: 15-20 computation problems.
- Finish with: 10-minute formula rewrite from memory.
- Goal: compute expectation and spread cleanly.
Day 4: Binomial and geometric distributions
- Review: when to use binomial vs geometric; parameters and shape.
- Practice: 20 problems mixed between identification and calculation.
- Finish with: 5 “which distribution?” classification questions.
- Goal: recognize distribution cues instantly.
Day 5: Normal distribution and z-scores
- Review: normal model, z-score, standardization, percentile interpretation.
- Practice: 18-20 normal-distribution questions.
- Finish with: 1 short mixed quiz on Days 1-5.
- Goal: convert values to z-scores and interpret area/probability.
Day 6: Distribution mix day
- Morning block: 35-minute review of all distribution types.
- Main block: 30-35 mixed problems on probability + distributions.
- Final block: build error log with categories: concept, setup, algebra, interpretation.
- Goal: connect topic selection to problem wording.
Day 7: Week 1 checkpoint
- Timed set: 45-60 minutes on Week 1 material.
- Review: correct every error and rewrite 5 hardest questions.
- Short review: update one-page formula sheet.
- Goal: score at least 70-75% untimed-adjusted accuracy.
Day 8: Estimation and confidence interval basics
- Review: parameter vs statistic, sampling variability, CI meaning.
- Practice: 15-18 confidence interval setup problems.
- Finish with: write a plain-English interpretation for 5 intervals.
- Goal: interpret intervals without common wording mistakes.
Day 9: Confidence intervals for means and proportions
- Review: when to use each interval type; margin of error.
- Practice: 18-22 calculation and interpretation questions.
- Finish with: identify conditions/assumptions for each problem.
- Goal: choose the right CI method quickly.
Day 10: Hypothesis testing foundations
- Review: null vs alternative, test statistic, p-value, significance level, Type I/II error.
- Practice: 15-20 setup questions before heavy computation.
- Finish with: explain hypothesis testing process aloud in 2 minutes.
- Goal: understand the logic before plugging into formulas.
Day 11: One-sample tests for means and proportions
- Review: test steps and rejection decisions.
- Practice: 18-20 full hypothesis test problems.
- Finish with: 5 conclusion-writing drills in context.
- Goal: write statistically correct conclusions, not just calculations.
Day 12: Confidence intervals vs hypothesis tests
- Review: relationship between CI and significance testing.
- Practice: 15-18 compare-and-decide problems.
- Finish with: mini mixed set from Days 8-11.
- Goal: know when each method answers the question best.
Day 13: Hypothesis testing intensive
- Main block: 25-30 mixed testing problems under moderate time pressure.
- Review block: classify every miss by error type.
- Short review: memorize a standard test workflow.
- Goal: reduce setup errors and conclusion errors.
Day 14: Week 2 checkpoint
- Timed quiz: 60-75 minutes on CIs + hypothesis testing.
- Review: redo every missed problem without notes.
- Short review: update formula sheet and decision checklist.
- Goal: be able to identify and complete common intro inference problems.
Day 15: Correlation basics
- Review: scatterplots, direction, form, strength, outliers, correlation interpretation.
- Practice: 15-20 interpretation questions.
- Finish with: distinguish correlation from causation in 5 examples.
- Goal: describe relationships clearly and cautiously.
Day 16: Simple linear regression concepts
- Review: regression line, slope, intercept, prediction, residual.
- Practice: 15-18 regression interpretation and calculation questions.
- Finish with: 5 “interpret the slope/intercept” drills.
- Goal: interpret coefficients in context.
Day 17: Regression and model fit
- Review: residuals, \(r\), \(r^2\), fit quality, extrapolation limits.
- Practice: 18-20 mixed correlation/regression problems.
- Finish with: 10-minute recap of common traps.
- Goal: connect graphs, equations, and interpretation.
Day 18: Full mixed review I
- Timed mixed set: probability, distributions, CI, tests, correlation, regression.
- Review: spend at least half the session on corrections.
- Final 10 minutes: formula recall from memory.
- Goal: identify weakest 2 topics for final repair.
Day 19: Weak-area repair day
- Review: only your weakest 2 topics from Day 18.
- Practice: 20-25 targeted problems.
- Finish with: 8 mixed problems to test transfer.
- Goal: turn weak topics into at least “safe” topics.
Day 20: Full mock exam
- Sit one full timed practice exam under exam conditions.
- Review every error; note whether issue was concept, setup, arithmetic, or wording.
- Create a final-page checklist: distributions, CI/test steps, regression interpretation.
- Goal: simulate the real exam and refine pacing.
Day 21: Final consolidation
- 30 minutes: formula sheet + test-selection review.
- 30-45 minutes: 8-12 easy-to-medium confidence-building problems.
- 20 minutes: review error log only, no new material.
- Final phase: rest and stop early.
- Goal: go into the exam clear, not overloaded.
Practice-First Revision Method
Use this structure for every   90-minute weekday  :
-   15 min   short review of notes or video/textbook summary
-   55 min   practice problems
-   15 min   correction and error log
-   5 min   formula/definition recall from memory
Use this structure for every   3-hour weekend day  :
-   30 min   fast review
-   90 min   larger practice set
-   30 min   correction and rework
-   20 min   mixed recall or mini-quiz
-   10 min   update formula sheet and error log
Best revision rules for your learning style:
-   Do problems before rereading theory.
-   Correct immediately   and write why the right method works.
- Keep one   error log   with 4 labels: concept, setup, algebra, interpretation.
- Build one   one-page formula sheet   and rewrite it from memory every 3-4 days.
- Every 3 days, do   5 mixed old problems   so earlier topics stay active.
- In the final week, spend   more time reviewing mistakes than reading notes  .
Exam-Focused Tactics
Priority order for scoring:
- Master   question identification   first: what topic is this?
- Then master   procedure  : what steps/formula apply?
- Then improve   speed and arithmetic accuracy  .
Fast decision cues:
-   Probability language  : chance, event, given, independent.
-   Distributions  : repeated independent trials, counts of success, waiting for first success, z-score/normal shape.
-   Confidence intervals  : estimate a parameter with a range.
-   Hypothesis tests  : test a claim using evidence and p-value.
-   Correlation/regression  : relationship between two quantitative variables, prediction, slope, \(r\), \(r^2\).
